I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. At 76, my knees give me trouble, my son works in Shijiazhuang and only comes back for harvest. I'm not going to try anything new or risky. I grow what I know and what the land here is good for: winter wheat, then summer maize on the same fields. That rotation is what everyone in this county does, what my father did. The ground is flat, the well is there, the seed station in town sells what I need.

I have about 5 mu. I'll plant all of it to wheat this winter, then follow with maize after June harvest — same fields, same rotation as always.

For wheat, I'll buy the improved jimai seed from the village supply station — I've used it three years running, it doesn't lodge and the yield is decent. I'll do a rotary tillage pass before planting since the soil gets compacted after maize. I'll apply compound fertilizer as base and urea in spring when the plants are jointing. Three irrigations: before winter freeze, jointing, and heading. Two pesticide sprays — one for aphids in spring, one for rust if it shows up.

For maize, I direct-seed into the stubble right after wheat harvest — saves me the tillage work at my age. Hybrid seed, I've used Xianyu 335 type before. One irrigation if July is dry. One pesticide pass for corn borer. I'll pull some potassium this time — the soil is getting tired.
